idiom_name: immutable case class with pure methods and a validating companion
implementation_notes: The Scala canon folds the model into immutable data: case classes (and enums or sealed traits for alternatives) with pure methods that return new instances, and a companion object holding smart constructors and validation - the hybrid FP/OOP style the Scala 3 book recommends when behaviour belongs with the data. Updates go through copy inside the methods, so invariants are re-checked on every transition and side effects stay outside the model. Choose the FP-first variant below when the team wants data and behaviour strictly separated.
pitfalls: A public constructor or public copy() lets callers assemble invalid states; make the constructor private and expose validated methods and factories.
Case-class equality is structural: entities with different identities but equal fields compare equal - override equals/hashCode or wrap the identity.
Immutable updates allocate (lines :+ line copies the list), so hot paths should use efficient persistent collections or builders rather than repeated O(n) appends.

variants.name: Skinny case classes with behaviour as pure functions
variants.idiom_name: case classes/enums as data + pure functions in the companion or extension methods
variants.implementation_notes: The FP-first realization keeps the model as data: case classes and enums with no methods, and behaviour as pure functions placed in the companion object, in 'functional object' methods, or in extension methods added later - the Scala 3 book's 'skinny domain objects'. Invariants migrate into smart constructors and into function signatures (total functions over the ADT, errors returned as values); the data+behaviour binding is deliberately looser than in the hybrid style, and behaviour that spans objects becomes plain functions over the model. Choose it when the codebase is FP-first or when the data must stay trivially inspectable.
pitfalls: Nothing stops callers from constructing invalid case classes directly; funnel creation through the smart-constructor functions (a private constructor is still allowed on a case class).
Without methods, name collisions and discoverability suffer: keep the functions in the companion or extension scope and export them deliberately.
Structural equality on entities persists in this variant as well - identity has to be made explicit.
